newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's LPMO buys 7,014 tonnes of frozen beef.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's LPMO buys 7,014 tonnes of frozen beef.

text.p: South Korea's state-run Livestock Products Marketing Organisation (LPMO) said on Wednesday it bought a total of 7,014 tonnes of frozen beef through tenders on March 7.
An LPMO official said it bought 2,626 tonnes of beef from the United States, 360 tonnes from Canada, 2,998 tonnes from Australia and 1,030 tonnes from New Zealand.
U.S. and Canadian chuck roll were bought at an average of $2,783 per tonne on a cost and freight basis, traders said.
Australian and New Zealand grass-fed fullset was bought at an average of $2,677 and grass-fed bone-in beef at an average of $1,729, they said.
Arrivals were set for Seoul (5,132 tonnes), Pusan (1,284 tonnes), Taegu (54 tonnes) and Naju (544 tonnes).
Delivery of 3,589 tonnes was slated for April 10 and 3,425 tonnes for April 20.
